about: How many signatures a candidate's petition asks, for every family of offices, where data/research/elections/filing-requirements.json gives the place's rule as a formula, a percentage, a floor, a ceiling, a count by town size or nothing. Read by petitionRule in src/core2/modules/elections.ts and computed for the race's own electorate by petitionNeededHere in src/core2/modules/voting.ts: the town's voters for a municipal office; the district's or the state's for a county, legislative, statewide or U.S. House office (owner, Nov 14: a race needs the number its own law sets for its own electorate, never a town's share). A side with no row here keeps what its research row gives: a fixed count, or none. Every row is ESTIMATED from its own text, quoted in `text`.
share: The fraction of the base the law asks. `base` is "registered" (registered voters) or "votes" (votes cast for the office or at the last election); the world keeps no voter rolls, so a registered base is the town's eligible voters times registeredShareOfEligible and a votes base the town's people times localElectorateShareOfPopulation (both in campaigns/parameters.json; the latter is a presidential year's, so it overstates a local election's); where the world has recorded the office's last election, a "votes" base reads those votes.

fields.base: registered | votes | eligible | population: registered voters (the electorate's eligible voters times registeredShareOfEligible), votes cast (`election`), eligible voters, or residents (the electorate's eligible voters times the town's own people per eligible voter)
fields.min: floor on the count, where the law sets one
fields.max: ceiling on the count, where the law sets one
fields.orFixed: the count when the law says the fixed number or the share, whichever is less
fields.byPopulation: fixed counts by the town's population: the first tier whose belowPopulation exceeds the town's applies; the tier without belowPopulation is for larger towns
fields.election: for a votes base, which recorded election it is: "office" (votes for the office being sought at its last election), "level" (the most votes cast in any one contest at the last election of the same level, the municipal election), or the kind of another office whose votes in the town the law counts ("governor", "secretary-of-state", "legislature-lower"): the town's own residents' votes (named and counted) at that office's last recorded election, which the town's world records for the offices that cover it. Before that race has been held in the run, or where the world seats no such office for the town, the base is sized from the town's people times the votes-cast share. For a county, district or state race the same names read the race's own electorate: "office" the votes recorded for the office being sought, or before it has been held in the run, the two-party votes its places last cast; "governor", "secretary-of-state", "president" and "us-house" the two-party votes its places last cast.
fields.count: a fixed count where the law's number is known but the research row did not hold it; 0 where the law asks no petition (a fee, an endorsement or a declaration files the candidate)
fields.party: true where the base is the candidate's own party's voters: the base times the share of the electorate on the candidate's side of the lean order (an even split for a candidate with no party)
fields.winner: true where the base is the votes for the last successful candidate: the larger side of the base
